q01.why: 6 facilities ranked by one MW metric; horizontal ranked bars beat columns (not a time series) and bk22 (no median needed)

q02.why: 4 markets on one unit (US$/kW/month), Singapore highlighted; ranked bar is the house ranking exhibit

q03.why: 4 takeaway points of commentary beside a deal exhibit; bullets fit several points, takeaway holds only one

q04.why: 4 interpretive points (cap rates, price/MW, accretion, implication) as commentary beside charts; bullets beat pills for so-what text

q05.why: One deal with mixed text and number terms (price, area, tenants, WALE, DPU) reads best as a term table

q06.why: 5 unrelated headline risk numbers in a row under a risk table; strip beats icons as numbers support the matrix

q07.why: 7-category industry mix, standalone vs combined company; before/after donuts show diversification better than one stacked bar

q08.why: One headline offer price ($13.25) with 3 supporting premiums; hero number beats an equal-weight strip

q09.why: 4 text points on financing structure beside the price panel; no term-sheet detail for bk47

q10.why: 7 peers with multiples (x) at several dates; table with inline bars follows the multiple-change precedent

q11.why: IRR sensitivity on two different driver pairs (entry/exit and price/leverage) = twin sensitivity tables

q12.why: 5 text projection points for one of two management cases; two-case comparison precedent

q13.why: EBITDA by 7 segments over 2023E-27E in US$mm = mix over time, stacked columns

q14.why: Equity value, EV and multiples at several prices = offer summary table across a price range

q15.why: 3 process options scored on 3 criteria with no numbers; Harvey balls show relative scoring best

q16.why: 3 alternatives (sell, hold, spin) compared on value cases and required growth; follows alternatives-comparison precedent

q17.why: 5x5 liquidity grid on revenue vs % of revenue; a plain sensitivity table fits $ sizing, not a return heatmap

q18.why: 6 customer verticals as names without detail plus a count; logo wall by vertical per the partners precedent

q19.why: 8 offer terms mostly text (confidence, contingencies, sponsors); bullet list beats an offer table with only one price

q20.why: 6 modelling assumptions of mixed measures, short lines; bullets beside the proposal, units too mixed to chart

q21.why: 5 headline financing metrics (WAM, WACD, flex, fees) in a row under the term sheet

q22.why: 6 annual values in $MM, one series; column fits a short market-size trend, too few points for line

q23.why: Premiums paid across precedents and VWAP measures with medians = premiums-paid exhibit

q24.why: Value per share by discount rate x multiple x dilution, 7 rows; one sensitivity table with unaffected reference

q25.why: 8 valuation ranges in $ per share against offers; classic football field

q26.why: Cost line items with $ and % of sales across 2024E-28E = bank-format financial table

q27.why: Two forecast cases compared on GWP and underwriting profit over years = plan vs plan chart grid

q28.why: 10 rows of price, premium, equity value, EV and multiples at successive offers = offer summary table

q29.why: 5 methods each with a description, no numbers = methodology overview

q30.why: 3 firm-size tiers (large, mid, small) with on-prem vs cloud coverage = pyramid of tiers

q31.why: Peers ranked on growth and margin each with a median; ranked columns with median line per metric

q32.why: Accretion/(dilution) % by year, P/E and equity share = merger impact grid

q34.why: 6 dated financing/covenant events alongside the process = calendar with key dates

q35.why: One sentence note on advisor role; a single framing line, not a list

q40.why: 5 APAC countries with MW capacity = Asia Pacific country map

q41.why: Exactly 2 cases, bull vs bear, short text each = two-way arrows

q42.why: 4 gaps the target fills = strategic-fit jigsaw pieces locking into a whole

q44.why: 6 equal capabilities, one word each = six hexagon pillars with icons
